revisions.reason: Before any matrix was written. The build was started at 12:30 PM CT and stopped by hand during its first position: build.jsonl does not exist and the model copy has the original file's sha256. Three corrections to the solver and one report. (1) The pull's ridge counted from the original matrix. After a bringing back its least point was then the original, which is outside: at layer 0's feed-forward the pull's first step was 0.9989 to 1.0000 of the way back at each of twelve ridges, every one cut at a bound (weight-research-perfomance read it in records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/choose-behind.jsonl). It now counts from the matrix the path starts from, which after a bringing back is the matrix as it was brought back; from the original the two are one, so a first matrix is solved as before. Astra decided the same center independently (records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-splitting-and-constrained-pull-astra.md); every trace bound still counts from the original. (2) The ridge of a bringing back is halved after every round that did not halve what is outside, in place of the projection on the rounds left, under which 14 of 19 rounds went by before the ridge had come down. (3) A round of a bringing back is 10 passes of 40 iterations in place of 5 of 80 (weight-research-perfomance's measurement: fewer rounds and a smaller change at two ridges). On the kept rows with all three: layer 0's feed-forward is back inside both merges in 10 rounds and 268 s, the ridge ending at 2^-15, with 2.21% of the matrix changed; layer 1's attention in 3 rounds and 24 s at the floor with 0.97% (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/back-behind-halved.out, position2-behind-halved.out). The report: this run's reference is controlled-bf16-2's in all 105 array files, byte for byte; reference/index.json differs in the last digits of reading_apart_rms (up to 3.1e-8 relative) and of the rebuilt merge's question parts (up to 4.8e-7), which are sums taken in another order (weight-research-perfomance's comparison). The prediction said the last digit; the arrays hold it, those sums do not. What the corrected pull changes in the prediction: at layer 1's attention on the kept rows a real pull now exists, the audited third's tube loss falling with the solved third's (0.87 to 0.92 left in both at the small ridges), and the audited third then leaves a bound at the answers' first places (the direction at place 0 at 1.03 to 1.15 of its bound, the size at place 2 at 1.09 to 2.09), so what is kept is small (0.9550 to 0.9537). The same is expected along the sweep: matrices keep pulls, small ones, limited by the audited third at those places. At layer 0's feed-forward the pull still keeps nothing (0.9103). No bound, target, floor or step of the method is changed.

A correction of the revision above, made while the first matrices were being written; nothing of the run is changed. That revision gave the pull kept at layer 1's attention on the kept rows as 0.9550 to 0.9537. Those are two records: with the pull's ridge counted from the path's start alone the bringing back left 0.955025 and 0.954959 was kept; with the bringing back's ridge halved as well it left 0.953725 and 0.953708 was kept (Astra's correction, from records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/position2-behind-anchored.jsonl and position2-behind-halved.jsonl). hypothesis: A capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, from where the two shared patterns part until they reconcile, and editing the weights where that difference lives repairs the capability. In the form this run tests: if each matrix is changed only as far as it brings the wrong answers' pattern toward the correct one where the two diverge, while every other part of the trace stays inside what the original model's own answers vary by, then the edited model, answering on its own, carries the wrong group's trace nearer the correct pattern over the divergence and leaves both groups' patterns, their spread, the questions' positions and the size of the state where the original model has them.
what_went_wrong_before: The four rungs of November 10 (a2-path, b2-path, c2-path with c2-protected, d2-path) built the edit at full strength and added protection afterwards, and none shows what the round has to show. a2-path moved its own traces 0.79 of the way along the gap over places 142 to 313 and about one gap to the side in both groups, completed 17 of the 30 wrong answers and broke 12 of the 30 correct ones. b2-path held the broken answers' rows on their given text and 4 of the 12 stayed complete: the model's own answers leave that text at the fourth token. c2-path and d2-path ended with 12 and 7 of the wrong answers complete. Four causes are on record. (1) Nothing bounded what moved where nothing was asked: the side movement was as large as the move. (2) The strength of each change was chosen by how much of the ask it met on the wrong answers' given text; nothing in that choice saw what the change did anywhere else. (3) The model file keeps a weight to about one part in 256, so a small change was mostly not written and the rest went in as whole steps: the same solve at layer 3's attention leaves 0.985 of the divergence in the file's format and 0.636 as float32 (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/path-bf16.jsonl, path-float32.jsonl). (4) A pass that reads an answer as given text is not the computation the model answers in: reading several tokens at once the engine rounds what goes into each matrix first, and the merge lies 0.0001 to 0.0007 from what the same weights give one token at a time (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/operator_cpu.out). (5) The first answer to (3) was the wrong one. controlled-sweep-1 kept the 70 matrices as float32 so that a small change could be written; Marcos rejected it before any fit (the problem is then the solver, and float32 is not acceptable; float32 is to be treated as if it had never existed), and the run was stopped with nothing fitted. The cause in (3) was in the solver: of 177 solves on record in the file's format, 153 ended with a step no part of which was kept and 24 at a bound (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/path-bf16.jsonl). A step written weight by weight either moved no weight the file holds, which the solver counted as a failure and answered by shrinking the step further, or moved some weights a whole BF16 step each, and that rounding alone put bounded parts of the trace 1.6 to 19 times past their bounds (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/bf16-writing.jsonl). Beside these, the rungs were judged by what the answers said, which Marcos set aside on November 10: the judge is the computational trace. controlled-bf16-1 (November 10 to 11), the first sweep under this rule, ended at its third matrix, not accepted, with the hypothesis not tested. Three causes are on record (its result.json; records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/README.md, the position2 rows and the five rows after them). (5) Layer 1 attention's merge stood outside its bounds once layer 0's changes were in the model, and the solver could not bring it back: its restoration aimed every part outside at no movement, refused steps cell by cell for the writing's own rounding, and took no step at 10 of 12 ridges. (6) What a solve read of a matrix was not what the engine read. Where the engine reads several tokens at once, at the question's positions and at each answer's first step, it rounds what goes into a matrix to the file's BF16 before multiplying, and a solve took those rows as recorded: a matrix the solve had inside every bound was read by the engine four parts past theirs at the answers' first place (3.68 times the direction's bound). (7) The build's one remedy, taking back the matrix written before, halved toward where that matrix stood, which after a bringing back is a matrix outside its own bounds, and it reaches one matrix back and no further. (8) The reference itself was in the form of (6): the overlap of the states it took its gap and chance from, the patterns and the direction variances were made from the original's recorded rows rebuilt from the input as recorded, and the size's expression floor kept part of that avoidable distance as an allowance (Astra, records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-native-reference-decision-astra.md). It stays that run's reference; it is not this one's. (9) controlled-bf16-2, November 11: with the reference and the solve in the engine's form the first matrix trained (layer 0's attention left 0.7727 of its tube loss) and the engine read each written matrix's own merge as the solve had. The sweep ended at its third matrix all the same: layer 0's feed-forward was brought back inside its own merge, and the merge behind it, the layer's last, where the engine adds the per-layer embedding, was left with five parts 0.4% to 11% past their bounds. No solve held that merge, no later matrix can move it, and the build's one remedy had nothing to take back, because the feed-forward kept no pull. Bringing the feed-forward back had taken 88 of the build's 93 minutes (studies/04-round-2-overlap/runs/controlled-bf16-2/result.json).
why_this_direction: Marcos's direction on what the training is stands as in controlled-bf16-1's declaration (journal/2026-11-10-controlled-training.md): protection inside the training, the trace and not the answers' text as the measure, BF16 throughout. His direction of November 11 says where the work is (journal/2026-11-11-reliable-training-configuration.md): the repairs and the transfer are established, and what is being derived is the configuration that reproduces them under control. This is the same step 5 again because the second sweep did not end on the method: it ended on a merge the solver did not hold. controlled-bf16-2's result names the remedy, the layer's last merge inside the feed-forward's solve, and that is now built and read on the case itself: the merge is a fixed function of the feed-forward's merge, rebuilt from the engine's source to float32's last digits on the original model and on the model that sweep left (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/layer-map-0.json, after-check.out), and with it held the choice at layer 0's feed-forward ends with every bound of both merges inside (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/choose-behind.out). The second thing that sweep showed, one bringing back taking 88 minutes, had one cause, the ridge, and is repaired the same way: measured on the kept rows, not assumed (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/README.md, the ridge of a bringing back). Nothing else is changed: the members, the target, the bounds, the floors, the reference's form and the tests are controlled-bf16-2's, made again here by this run's own commands from the same original observations. A sweep from the original file is the next step and not another repair on kept rows because the kept rows hold two matrices' worth of evidence; what a third and later matrix needs is only read by getting there, and Marcos asked on November 11 that what happens to the model be recorded as we go so the settings can be tuned from it: this build's record keeps every round and pass of every bringing back with its seconds, and weight-research-perfomance's as-we-go reading reads the checkpoints beside it without choosing anything.
repeating_pattern_check: What has happened more than once, why, and what this run does about each. (a) An edit moved the trace where nothing was asked, in every rung: nothing held those parts while a matrix was solved. Here every part of the trace has a bound from the original answers' own variance and every step of every solve is cut where a bound would be left. (b) A reading during the build did not predict the model's own answers, four times: the rows read were the wrong answers' own, on given text. Here the fitting answers are in three groups, a change is solved on one, held by the second and read on the third within that solve; the third affects stopping/selection, and across rotations every fitting member participates in construction. Half of the answers enter no fit, but their repeated development readings are not untouched independent confirmation; every pass feeds the answer's own tokens one at a time; and the test is the model's own answers, read by the trace alone. (c) The strength of an edit was a number taken or tuned (full strength, a ridge chosen by the ask alone, a floor from eight requests). Here no strength is chosen: a change stops where a bound or a read group stops it. (d) A result was read off the answers' text and the trace came second; Marcos corrected this more than once. Here no text, token or score enters any verdict, and what the answers say is reported beside the verdicts without deciding anything. (e) This session reacted to a rung's numbers by building the next rung. This run is not an answer to a number: it is the first run of the training Marcos asked for, and its prediction is written before it. (f) On the answers no fit used, single cells end past their bound while the fitting answers hold: one size cell of 960 at 1.55 of its bound at layer 3's attention (wrong group, place 151, a move asked there; the fitting answers read 0.43 at that cell), and two direction cells at layer 7's attention, 1.42 and 1.06 of their bounds where the fitting answers read 0.60 and 0.66. It is the same split between fitted and unfitted rows as (b), small and measured. The run does not widen a bound for it: Astra's ruling keeps the replay's limits as they are, and those answers have been read after every development row, so they are not an untouched test either; the replay says whether such cells stay, grow or wash out in the composed model. (g) This session took a number from a construction that is not the method's as its yardstick: after the float32 trial was stopped it reported the BF16 solver by how close it came to float32 readings, and Marcos named it drift: float32 is to be treated as if it had never existed, and it is not even known to be a good target. Nothing in this run is judged against a float32 reading or a converted copy: the reference is the original BF16 file, a candidate is a BF16 matrix, and progress is the tube loss left on the trace inside every bound. The controller refuses a run declared on a converted copy. (h) A solve stalled in the file's format, 153 times of 177, because a step that moved no stored weight was treated as a step that failed. A written matrix that equals the one stood on is now told apart from one that left a bound, and a step is written as a whole. (i) Work was lost to the machine: a power cut at 8:28 PM CT on November 10 ended every process and left a Git object empty. The build puts a cut position back as the file held it before it goes on, so the model file is always what its log describes, and every written matrix and record is on the disk before the next thing relies on it. (j) A reading the solver trusted was not what the engine did, twice: the float32 reading in (g), and the merge rebuilt from a matrix's input as recorded, which is not what the engine multiplies where it reads several tokens at once. Both times the yardstick was something other than the engine's own output of the original BF16 file. Here everything is counted from that output, the solve's expression of the merge is checked against it at every matrix of the original file before the sweep, and in the build every written matrix is read through the engine at the next position with the solve's reading of it beside it in the record. The same form sat in a third place, the reference and the overlap it is aimed at; both are made again here in the engine's form before any matrix is written, and what changed against the first ones is recorded, rises and falls alike, with nothing chosen between them. (k) A search ended where its fallback could not go, twice in one night: the restoration that took no step at 10 of 12 ridges, and the take-back that halved toward a matrix outside its own bounds. Here the bringing back is a solve of its own with the bounds as constraints, and a pull is taken back toward the matrix as it was brought back. (l) The layer's last merge is in no solve. It is the feed-forward's merged state plus the per-layer embedding, which the engine gates by that state (per_layer_inp_gate, GELU, the token's per-layer embedding, per_layer_proj and an RMS norm in the engine's gemma4 graph), so a feed-forward matrix inside every bound of its own merge can leave it outside: 1.35 of a bound at layer 0 in the first sweep. This run does not avoid that. It reads that merge through the engine after every feed-forward matrix and takes the pull back by halves, 12 passes each time; if a feed-forward matrix with no pull left to take back leaves it outside, the sweep ends there and says so. The remedy then is that merge's bounds inside the feed-forward's solve, which is not built. (m) This session repaired the solver for hours on kept rows before it read what the engine does with the repaired matrix, and the engine's reading then showed the second cause. From here a solver change that claims to hold a bound is read through the engine on the case before it is called done; in this run the build does that at every matrix. (n) Twice now a sweep ended at its third matrix, each time because the solve's picture of what the engine reads was short of the engine: the input's rounding at the rows read together (controlled-bf16-1), then a merge no solve held (controlled-bf16-2). What this run does about it: every merge the engine reads between two of our matrices is now inside some solve (the attention's merge in the attention's, the feed-forward's and the layer's last in the feed-forward's), and behind every written feed-forward the build reads the engine's own output while that matrix can still be chosen again. What it does not rule out: a third kind of shortfall at a later layer. If the sweep ends early again the record says at which merge and by how much, and that is read before any repair. (o) After a bringing back the pull has gained nothing at layer 0's feed-forward in every form tried: the path's starts are cut at a bound or leave one in the audited answers, and the bringing back alone is kept (0.910 of the tube loss left). This run does not avoid that; it measures it at every matrix. Under the allowances as they are, a matrix that arrives outside may end as a bringing back with little pull, and the tube loss left at the last merge would then be close to what the first matrices leave. Astra's proposed split of the mean and the row allowance (records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-mean-and-row-preservation-astra.md) is with Marcos through the President and is not used here. (p) I fixed a setting from one case and it was wrong on the next: the smallest ridge ended layer 0's feed-forward in 53 seconds and then changed layer 1's attention by 11.7% where the floor's ridge changes it by 1%. The ridge of a bringing back is therefore not a number of this declaration but a rule read from each round's own rate (parameters, ridge_of_a_bringing_back), and both kept cases were run with it before this was declared.

rule.members: The 60 registered answers of the overlap, 30 correct and 30 wrong (first incorrect calculation: the descent subtracted), with every generated step and every question position: 30,546 answer steps and 10,319 question rows. The fitting answers are every other answer of each group in the answers' own order, 15 and 15, in three groups of 5 and 5; the other 15 and 15 enter no fit. The patterns and all reference variances come from the original 30 and 30. Replay allowances use the reference count 30; native own-generation mean budgets use the evaluated count, 15 per group in the deciding cohort.
rule.model: The original file's own BF16. The run writes into a copy of the original file, made by `start` and equal to it byte for byte until the first matrix is written; the 70 attention-output and feed-forward-down matrices stay BF16 in it, and a matrix is written only as BF16 values the file holds exactly. No converted copy of the model exists in this run, and every movement is counted from the original BF16 file.
rule.target: At each matrix's merge, where the two original patterns of the state's direction lie further apart than two halves of one group do (gap > 2 chance), the wrong group's mean state is asked to move to the nearest point of the ball around the correct pattern whose radius is sqrt(2 chance). Inside the ball, and where the patterns follow each other, nothing is asked. The tube loss is the squared distance still outside the ball, summed over the asked places. The gap and its chance are those of state-overlap-2, the overlap of the states with a matrix's input taken as the engine multiplied it.
rule.bounds: At each place of the axis and each merge, for each group: the mean over its members of the squared movement of the unit state (the wrong group's after taking out their shared movement along the gap where a move is asked), and the same for the log of the state's size; for each question, the mean squared movement over its prompt positions, state and size. Each is held to the variance of the original group's members there over their number, 30, and never to less than how far the engine's own output of the original file, in the pass controlled-bf16-1 kept (its baseline), lies from the recorded rows. The recorded rows of a matrix's merge are rebuilt from the matrix's input as the engine multiplied it. They are this run's own reference, made by its reference command before any matrix is written; its sha256 goes into every reading's record.
rule.fit: One matrix at a time, on the model's own expression of the merge with the learned scale and both projections inside. A step is first-order through the merge; every bounded part pushes back with a strength that grows as it nears its bound; the step is then written into the file's BF16 from the matrix the solve stands on, the written matrix is put through the merge itself, every row's movement is measured, and the part of the step that keeps every bound and leaves less tube loss is found by halving: as finely as a linear solve resolves until a part holds, and to an eighth of the step between that part and one that fails (parameters, bracket). A part that moves no weight the file holds is recognized as that and is not a failure. A solve starts inside every bound: a merge that stands outside when its matrix is reached is brought back first (brought_back). Every state of a solve is a BF16 matrix; no finer copy of the weights is kept. The ridge of a pull counts from the matrix its path of ridges starts from: the matrix as the earlier changes left it, or as it was brought back (revisions, November 11). Every bound counts from the original, as before.
rule.written: How a step becomes BF16 weights. BF16 keeps a weight to about one part in 256 and most of what a step asks of a weight is under half of that, so the step is written as a whole: the input coordinates in the file's own order, each weight to its nearest BF16 value by the engine's rounding, and what a coordinate's rounding left over carried onto the coordinates not yet written, in the measure the step was solved in (what the bounds see of the matrix's inputs on the solved rows, plus the stage's ridge). Along the one output direction the size bounds see most, what they see is added to that measure; one direction is a declared approximation (parameters, size_directions_in_the_writing). A mean of three branch ends is written the same way, in the mean of their measures (the size part of each weighted by how far its direction agrees with the common one, an approximation the record labels). A factorization that fails ends the solve; nothing is damped to make it pass. What is written is then read like any trial: the writing proposes, the bounds decide.
rule.choose: Which matrix is kept is decided inside the fitting answers (Astra, November 10, 'BF16 candidate selection and size-aware writing' in records/retrospectives/2026-11-10-stable-training-review-astra.md). Three branches go along one path of ridges that starts at the matrix's own unit and is halved stage by stage; in each branch one third of the fitting answers is solved on (the pull is theirs and their bounds push back), a second third's bounds push back in the solve as well with no pull of theirs and must hold at every step, and the last third is only read after each step; each branch starts a stage from where its last one ended. A branch stops at the first matrix whose read group, or all the fitting answers together, leaves a bound, and keeps its last matrix inside; the other branches go on. The candidates are the matrix the path started from, every branch's end of every stage that ended inside, a stopped branch's last matrix inside, and a stage's mean, written as a whole, where all three of its ends are inside. Each candidate is read as itself on the three thirds and on all the fitting answers together and must hold every bound in all four readings. Among those, the one that leaves all the fitting answers together the least tube loss is kept; on an exact tie the least in its worst third, then the smallest change from where the path started. Nothing is changed unless less tube loss is left than the matrix as it stands leaves. The thirds are construction data, not tests.
rule.sweep: The 70 matrices in path order (layer 0 attention, layer 0 feed-forward, layer 1 attention, and so on), from the original file, each solved on what arrives with the earlier changes in the model, read by a pass through the model with the fitting answers' own tokens fed one at a time. The same pass reads what the engine itself puts out at the merges just above, which no later matrix can move: after attention the attention's merge; before the next layer's attention the feed-forward's merge and the layer's last merge. If a bound is outside there, or nothing brings this matrix's own merge back inside, the pull of the matrix written just before is taken back by halves toward where that pull started (that matrix as it stood, or as it was brought back) until it holds. Where nothing can be taken back, or no part holds, the sweep ends there and is not accepted; the model is kept as it stands for inspection. The build can be cut off and run again: it goes on after the last matrix whose record is in its log, a position that was cut off while it wrote is first put back as the file held it, and a matrix written before the restart can no longer be taken back. From this run on the layer's last merge is also held inside the feed-forward's solve and read behind the written feed-forward before the next matrix is reached (rule, behind); the reading before the next layer's attention stays, with its remedy as it was.
rule.replay: The finished model read once on the 15 and 15 answers no fit used, their own tokens fed one at a time, at all 105 merges from the engine's own output, counted from the original file's. The replay passes if every bound holds at every merge and the tube loss, summed over the merges, is less than the original file's own reading leaves by the same reference. Nothing is chosen from it.
rule.own_answers: The test. The original file and the finished model each answer the 60 questions with nothing supplied, greedy, to the limit the recordings were made with. Each answer is laid on the frozen axis by its computation alone and read at all 105 merges: the tube on the wrong pattern; for each group at each place and merge how far its pattern moved and how far the spread of its members around the original centre changed, for the state and for its size; each question's prompt rows. Each of the four is held to twice the original answers' variance of that quantity over the number of answers in the mean read, 15 a group on the answers no fit used, which decide, and never to less than what the original file's second set of answers reads against its first. The own answers hold if every answer is whole as its recording was (parameters, answer_limit; whether every answer ended by itself is on record beside it as the plain fact), every budget and prompt bound holds at every merge, and the tube loss is less than the original reference loss (normalized loss 1 for this first sweep). The original file's second answers supply the fixed own-generation fidelity floors and a separate no-edit loss diagnostic, not the progress comparator. No text, token or score enters.
rule.verdict: The replay and the own answers are two verdicts, read in either order, and stay two (Astra, November 10, 'Replay decision after ordering removal' in records/retrospectives/2026-11-10-stable-training-review-astra.md). The sweep is eligible for a next one when both hold for the same model, the same frozen reference and the same answers. The own answers holding while the replay fails is a finding about the model's own traces with the failed replay beside it; it is not an eligible sweep and it does not show the answers were damaged. The repair of the pattern is whole only if, beyond that, no asked place is left outside its ball. This is a statement about the recurring pattern of the trace on these answers, not that every answer is right.
rule.what_is_frozen: Everything the original model fixes is written once, from the original model alone, before any matrix is written, and only read after. The reference (patterns, bounds, floors) is made by this run's reference command from the original's recorded rows, rebuilt as the engine multiplied them, the engine's own output in controlled-bf16-1's baseline and state-overlap-2. The budgets of the own answers and their floors are made by this run's own-start command from the original file's two sets of answers, under this reference, with their sha256 checked at the reading. Everything is counted from the engine's own output of the original file in that baseline. No edited model enters any of them, and they are not made again once made, whatever they allow or do not allow at any matrix (Astra: 'Freeze F under the existing rule, independently of whether it rescues layer 0'; 'A fresh derived reference is frozen once made'). Beside them, choosing nothing: what changed against controlled-bf16-1's reference and floors, rises and falls alike (reference-against-controlled-bf16-1.json).
rule.what_only_bounds_the_work: Five layers to a pass only bounds the raw stream on disk; the rows read are the same however they are grouped. The solver's caps and spacing are parameters below. The writing of a step carries the leftovers of 128 coordinates at a time on to the later ones in one product: the same recursion with its sums in another order, and in every comparison made the same matrix bit for bit (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/carried-blocks.out). From November 11, before any matrix was written: the writing measure's factor comes from one factorization in place of three (the same upper factor of the same symmetrized matrix; Astra checked the algebra), its sums are taken one matrix at a time in the order they were written in, and a branch's basis and the earlier stages' matrices wait off the card between their uses. The solver as declared had not been run at the 20 matrices that are 12288 wide, and there it ran out of the card's memory in its first solve (weight-research-perfomance's reading). No rule differs; the roundings inside the factor do, and layer 3's attention reads 0.4767 through it against 0.4765 and 0.4766 before (lines 19, 14, 17 of the development record). On the card a step is written by pipeline/weight_edit/fused.py: the solver's own operations on every element in the solver's own order, launched as three kernels a coordinate in place of about thirty. It wrote the loop's weights bit for bit at all four widths of the model's matrices (records/development/2026-11-10-speed-review/fused-writing/card.log), and layer 3's attention reads 0.4687 through it against 0.4685 and 0.4687 through the loop (lines 27, 22, 26). The loop stays in tube.py as what it is checked against and as what runs without a card. Its kernels are compiled by the library's own, private, compiler of small kernels, so they are checked again after any change of the library (the check is check.py beside that log). From November 11, after the build stopped at its second matrix: the size bounds' part of the writing measure is kept as it was summed, in double precision, off the card. Every BF16 solver before had kept it in float32, and rounded so it is not the matrix the measure is made of once the stage's ridge is small against the rounding: at layer 0's feed-forward its entries reach 2.6e7, the rounding alone has eigenvalues from -1.42 to 0.57, and at ridge 0.40 (the unit halved seven times) the measure's smallest eigenvalue is -0.24 with the float32 part and 0.40, the ridge, with the double one. Of the 42 measures of that matrix's solve the float32 one cannot be factored at 10 and the double one at none (line 28 of the development record and its MEASURE lines). Nothing is added to the measure and no rule differs.
rule.what_a_rerun_would_repeat: Sums on the card are not taken in one fixed order, so no two runs of a solve are the same run. The bringing back alone, run 17 times from one start on two cards since its last repair, ended inside every time, in three to eight rounds, at matrices that differ (changed by 0.43 to 0.71% of the matrix, all the fitting answers together at 0.972 to 0.989 of their furthest bound). A branch of a pull ends on a threshold. A second run of this sweep would hold the same bounds and need not keep the same matrix at any position: what the run shows is one outcome of the procedure.
rule.beside_the_verdicts: What the two models write to the 60 questions is scored as in the round's scoring and reported beside the verdicts; it decides nothing (Marcos, November 10). Reserved-40b stays sealed.
rule.original_observations: What the original file was observed to do is read where controlled-bf16-1 keeps it and never written: its own output at every one of the 105 merges on all 60 answers' own text, read as generated (baseline, with the sha256 of the file read in its index), and its second answers to the 60 questions (own/original, 60 of 60 token for token the recorded ones). They are observations of the unchanged file and stay what they are whatever is counted from them. The reference's index and own/start.json of this run name them with their sha256. Nothing derived there is used here: not its reference, not its floors, not its record of the second answers.
rule.as_the_engine_multiplies: A solve reads a trial matrix through the merge rebuilt from the matrix's input and the state it adds to, with the input as the engine multiplies it (tube.multiplied): rounded to the file's BF16 at the rows the engine reads several tokens at once, which read as generated are the question's positions and each answer's first step (decided at the prompt's last position), and as recorded at every later step. The rebuilt merge and the engine's own output of a written matrix are both counted from the engine's own output of the original file in the first sweep's baseline. Nothing of the model or its execution is changed by this: it is the solver's arithmetic made the engine's. The original's recorded rows are rebuilt the same way for the reference (tube.recorded) and for the overlap it is aimed at (ladder.states).
rule.brought_back: A merge that an earlier change left outside a bound when its matrix is reached is brought back before anything pulls, on the three thirds of the fitting answers and on all of them together. A round's step is the least step from the matrix as it stands whose rows hold every bound to first order (Astra, November 11, 'A well-posed subproblem at a binding bound', with nothing pulling), found by splitting the rows from the step; it is written into the file's BF16 like any step and read through the merge itself. A part of a step is taken when the written matrix reads less outside in all. A part brought back is aimed inside its bound by the most any writing of this solve was measured to leave there, which is headroom for the next writing and no certificate (Astra). The ridge starts at the path's floor, where the change a bringing back leaves in the matrix is least, and is halved for the next round, down to the smallest ridge float32 tells from the unit, after every round that did not halve what is outside, or of which no part left less outside (parameters, ridge_of_a_bringing_back). The solve ends inside only when every bound of every third and of all together is inside, read at the written weights against the bounds as they are; otherwise the matrix is left as it stood and reported outside. A matrix that was brought back may pull like any other from there, and one at which no pull is kept stays as it was brought back (Astra, records/retrospectives/2026-11-11-restoration-and-progress-astra.md).
rule.behind: A feed-forward matrix is the last of ours before its layer's last merge, where the engine adds the per-layer embedding to the feed-forward's merge: pe_out = pe_in + post_norm * rmsnorm((gelu(pe_in @ inp_gate) * t) @ proj), t the token's per-layer input, fixed for a token and a layer (the engine's gemma4 graph). A feed-forward's solve reads that merge too, for every trial matrix, through the engine's own arithmetic (tube.Behind), and holds its bounds like its own merge's: in a bringing back, in every step of a pull, and in which matrix is kept. Its bounds are the reference's, as they are. After a feed-forward matrix is written the build reads the engine's own output at both merges. If the engine reads the layer's last merge outside where the solve read it inside (the engine rounds a state at the rows it reads together, and a rebuilt state can round the other way), the bounds the solve works to there are drawn in by the difference measured, never out (tube.Trace.against), and the matrix is chosen again from the one written, until the engine's reading is inside or the rounds allowed are used. What counts is always the engine's own reading against the bounds as they are; if it is still outside, the sweep ends at that matrix and is not accepted.

asked.derivation: gap > 2 * chance at a place and merge, where gap is squared pattern distance and chance = V_correct/30 + V_wrong/30. For either original group g, two complementary 15-member halves have expected squared mean contrast 4*V_g/30. Averaging that contrast scale across the two groups gives 2*chance. This is the frozen reference-resolution policy for asking a move, not a significance test or proof that a smaller discrepancy is absent.
asked.scales_with: the number of members in each group and their spread at that place and merge

ball.derivation: radius sqrt(2 * chance) around the correct pattern at each asked place and merge. Its squared radius is the average complementary-half contrast scale of the correct and wrong original groups, not the correct group's variance alone and not the expected distance itself. The nearest point of this ball is the declared target-resolution policy; it is not a confidence region for the correct centre.
ball.scales_with: the number of members in each group and their spread at that place and merge

bound.derivation: For each group, place and merge: the sample variance over the group's 30 members of the member's mean unit state there, summed over the coordinates, divided by 30; the same for the mean log size. The variance-over-count is an estimated group-mean variation scale used here as a conservative engineering allowance for same-history row-squared movement. It is not a confidence interval, a calibrated test of that row statistic, or proof that a movement below it is indistinguishable from sampling. For a question: at every place of the prompt the variance of its group's questions over 30, and over the question's positions the mean of that (Astra, records/retrospectives/2026-11-10-stable-training-review-astra.md).
bound.scales_with: the number of members in each group and their spread at that place and merge

reading_floor.derivation: No bound is less than what the readings themselves resolve, measured as the bound is, squares first: how far the engine's own output in the pass through the original file that controlled-bf16-1 kept (its baseline) lies from the rows recorded while the original model generated; for the size, how far the file's expression of the merge, rebuilt from the matrix's input as the engine multiplied it, lies from the size the engine recorded; at the last layer's last merge, where no prompt row was recorded, how far two readings of the prompts through the original file lie apart. Each bound is the larger of its variance term and this. It is measured from the original file only: an edited model's noise widens nothing.
reading_floor.scales_with: the engine build, the card and how a pass reads; measured again for another model or machine

fitting_half.derivation: Every other answer of each group in the answers' own order, 15 of 30. With n answers fitted and 30 - n only read, the sampling variance of what each side shows goes as 1/n and 1/(30 - n); the larger of the two is least at n = 15. The order is the registration's own, fixed before any fit.
fitting_half.scales_with: the number of members in each group

three_groups.derivation: Every third of the fitting answers within each group, 5 and 5 each. A change is solved on answers, held by other answers and read on answers no step used: three roles that must not share an answer need three groups, three is the least number that gives each role its own, and equal sizes by the same argument as the half. Each group takes each role once.
three_groups.scales_with: the number of fitting answers in each group

ridge_unit.derivation: Where the path of ridges starts, per matrix: the mean, over the directions a change can take, of the bounds' own push-back on the fitting rows before anything has moved, with each place's strength set so that every place at its bound costs as much as every ask unmet (the original tube loss over twice the number of places). Computed from the matrix's rows at the time it is solved; it places the path, and where the path ends is decided by the bounds and the read groups.
ridge_unit.scales_with: the matrix, its rows after the earlier changes, the bounds and the tube loss at its merge

own_budget.derivation: For each group, place and merge and each of the four quantities (the pattern's direction, its log size, the spread of the members' directions around the original centre, the spread of their log sizes): twice the original 30 answers' sample variance of that quantity over the number of answers in the mean that is read, 15 a group on the answers no fit used. The factor two and count 15 give the reference scale of a contrast between complementary original 15-member halves (or equally sized independent-reference means). They do not claim that the actual paired E/O contrast has variance 2V/15: that contrast also depends on E's variance and E/O covariance. This is a frozen reference-resolution policy, not a confidence guarantee. A model that words an answer differently is not held row by row: another answer of the same group lies about 60 times a row's replay bound away with both patterns unchanged (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/own-check-rows.out; the check of this budget is own-check.out beside it).
own_budget.scales_with: the number of answers in the mean read and the original answers' spread of each quantity

own_floor.derivation: No budget is less than what the original file does not repeat: the same four quantities read on a second set of the original BF16 file's own answers to the same questions against the recordings, on the same cohort and through the same registration (the second answers controlled-bf16-1 keeps under own/original, read where they are; this run's own/original-floors.npz, made under this run's reference). Made only if every one of those answers is whole as its recording was (answer_limit) and the capture was made as the recordings were; never from an edited model.
own_floor.scales_with: the engine build, the card and the recorder; measured again for another model or machine

answer_limit.derivation: 768 tokens, the limit every one of the 60 original recordings was made with (max_tokens there). Three of the recordings ran into it: expanded-001-h1, expanded-001-h3 and expanded-044-h1 (ended false, stopped_limit true and 768 steps in their result.json under runs/wide-overlap/capture). An answer is whole as its recording was when it ended by itself within the limit, or, where the recording itself ran into the limit, when it did that or ran into the same limit; either way with every decision it made kept at every merge the recording keeps. An answer that stopped any other way, or whose capture is short, is never whole. Nothing is counted from a set that has an answer which is not whole. Whether every answer ended by itself stays on record as the plain fact. Until November 11 this read 'An answer that runs into it is not a whole answer, and nothing is counted from a set that has one', which asked of every answer what three of the recordings never did (Astra's correction: 'Reference-relative observation completeness' in records/retrospectives/2026-11-10-stable-training-review-astra.md).
answer_limit.scales_with: the limit of the recordings the answers are compared with

resolved.derivation: sqrt of float32's epsilon, approximately 0.000345, where float32 is the arithmetic the rows are recorded in and a step is solved in, not a format of the model: the relative linear-residual stopping tolerance, the minimum remaining-bound fraction in the barrier weights, and the lowest relative ridge visited. Computing this value from epsilon does not derive the square-root choice from model evidence or prove that smaller remainders are numerically unresolvable. This is a numerical setting with an explicit calibration gap, not a trace allowance; its roles must not be conflated with the independently checked feasibility bounds.
resolved.scales_with: the arithmetic the rows are recorded and solved in

size_directions_in_the_writing.derivation: 1. The size bounds' action on a written matrix's leftover is a moment over output directions; the writing's measure takes its top eigenvector alone, with that eigenvector's own action on the inputs. One is the least number of directions that lets the writing see the size bounds at all, and more than one would need the cross terms between directions, which the coordinate-by-coordinate writing does not carry exactly (Astra: 'do not extend to several eigenvectors as exact'). At layer 3's attention that one direction holds 0.818 of the moment; with it, the size as written reads 0.15 to 0.43 of its bound over the steps of the solves, where without it it read 0.16 to 0.999, and the fitting answers are left 0.544 of their tube loss against 0.918 (lines 6 and 4 of the record, counted from 1). The share it holds is recorded for every solve. It is an approximation inside the proposal of a written matrix; every written matrix is read against the unchanged bounds whatever it proposes. Not chosen from the answers no fit used.
size_directions_in_the_writing.scales_with: how much of what the size bounds see lies along one output direction at that matrix; recorded per solve as size_direction_share

iterations_of_a_linear_solve.derivation: 80. A cap on the solver's work, not a bound on the trace: a solve cut short is a smaller or less well aimed step, never a step outside a bound, since what is inside is read from the merge at the written weights. It was 40 when the run was declared and was read at its neighbours in the file's BF16 before any matrix was written (the record's lines counted from 1; the numbers are the fitting answers' pooled tube loss left inside every bound, and work is counted in iterations and writings because seconds on this machine move with what other sessions run). Layer 3's attention: 0.4905 at 20 (line 13); 0.4928, 0.4884, 0.4848 and 0.4872 at 40 (lines 8, 16, 20, 18, which differ in the bracket only); 0.4765, 0.4766 and 0.4767 at 80 (lines 14, 17, 19: one setting three times, which is what a repeat on the card moves); through the solver that builds 0.4685 at 80 (line 22; 0.4687 in lines 26 and 27) with 15,520 iterations in all, and 0.4432 at 160 (line 24) with 31,040. What a linear solve leaves of its slope there, median of a stage's solves after 40, 80 and 160 iterations: 0.016 to 0.05, 0.006 to 0.015 and 0.002 to 0.005 at ridges 2^0 to 2^-4; 0.26 to 0.54, 0.07 to 0.22 and 0.035 to 0.046 at 2^-6 and 2^-7, where the bounds bind (lines 17, 22, 24). Layer 11's feed-forward: 0.6171 at 40 (line 10), 0.6086 at 80 (line 23). Layer 15's feed-forward, 12288 wide like 20 of the 70 matrices: 0.2835 and 0.291 at 80 (line 21, and the timed run in records/development/2026-11-10-speed-review/solver-build/) with 6,320 and 6,156 iterations in 1,036 and 1,340 s; 0.2944 at 160 (line 25) with 14,720 iterations in 1,901 s. So 40 cuts the solve short where the bounds bind, and 80 is taken. 160 gains 0.025 at layer 3's attention and nothing at the widest matrix, for about one and a half times the seconds on the matrices that are most of a sweep; it is not taken for this build. No cap read is the solve's own stop: at 160 a twentieth of the slope is still left where the bounds bind. Why the linear solve is that slow was looked for and not found: seven other preconditioners were read beside the solve (line 26) and none leaves less of the slope at every ridge. The answers no fit used choose nothing here.
iterations_of_a_linear_solve.scales_with: the matrix's width, how unevenly its rows weigh on a change, and how well the preconditioner fits the objective where the bounds bind; measured again for another model

rounds_of_a_stage.derivation: 40. A cap on the solver's work: a solve of a stage ends when a step gains nothing, and after at most 40 rounds it hands where it stands to the next stage, which starts from there, so reaching it loses nothing that was gained. In the record's first eight lines 121 solves took a median of 4 rounds, 17 at the 95th percentile and at most 26; none reached 40.
rounds_of_a_stage.scales_with: how slowly a matrix's solves gain near their bounds

spacing_of_the_ridges.derivation: The ridge is halved from one stage to the next. The factor only spaces the stages tried along one path; it is no bound on the trace. What is kept is no longer a whole stage: a branch that leaves a bound keeps its last matrix inside within that stage, and every stage's ends and mean are candidates, so the spacing sets how often a candidate is offered, not how far a change may go. At layer 3's attention the candidates of neighbouring stages differ by 0.04 to 0.08 of the tube loss (line 8). Read quartered at layer 3's attention before any matrix was written (line 15): the fitting answers are left 0.4641 of their tube loss in 5 stages and 537 writings of the matrix, against 0.4928 in 9 stages and 952 halved (line 8). One matrix, one reading; and since a branch starts a stage from its own last end, a coarser spacing is another path, not fewer samples of the same one (Astra). It stays halved for this build, and is read at a feed-forward matrix before it is changed.
spacing_of_the_ridges.scales_with: nothing in the traces; a finer spacing costs a stage's solves for every stage added

bracket.derivation: How closely the part of a step that holds every bound is bracketed by halving. Until a part holds: as closely as a linear solve resolves (sqrt of float32's epsilon, twelve halvings), because a solve ends when no part of a step holds and must not be ended by a search that stopped early (Astra, November 11: with one bracket of 1/8 the parts 1, 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 can fail where 1/16 holds and gains, and the solve ends). Once a part holds: to an eighth of the step between it and a part that fails. A solve goes on from the part it took, so a part taken short costs it a round and not the result. Read at layer 3's attention with one bracket for the whole search, at 40 iterations: sqrt eps, eight times wider, 1/64 and 1/8 leave the fitting answers 0.4928, 0.4884, 0.4848 and 0.4872 of their tube loss with 952, 848, 620 and 372 writings of the matrix (lines 8, 16, 20, 18). Through the search as it now is, at 80 iterations: 0.4685 with 554 writings (line 22), against 0.4765 to 0.4767 with 724 to 774 writings when every search went to sqrt eps (lines 14, 17, 19). A change taken back in a build is still bracketed to sqrt eps: nothing goes on from there, so what is given up stays given up. It is a chosen resolution of a search, not a least distinguishable step: in the file's format a part of a step either moves stored weights or does not, and a part that moves none is recognized as that. It decides how much of a step is used, never whether the part used holds: that is read through the merge at the stored weights and in the end from the engine's own output.
bracket.scales_with: the arithmetic a step is solved in, and how many rounds a solve can spend on a part taken short

ridge_of_a_bringing_back.derivation: No fixed number. A bringing back starts at the matrix's unit times 2^-11, the path's floor (the last power of two at which the ridge is still more of the unit than a linear solve resolves; parameters, resolved). After every round that was taken and did not halve what is outside, and after one of which no part left less outside, the ridge is halved for the next round; it goes no lower than the unit times 2^-23, float32's epsilon. The half is the scheme's own step: ridges, steps and parts are halved everywhere in this solver. With the bounds as constraints the ridge does not set where the least step lies; it sets how far a round reaches a passed bound, whose rows are held with a stiffness of one over the bound, and how much change the splitting leaves in the matrix. Measured on the two kept cases: fixed at 2^-11, layer 0's feed-forward took 22 rounds and 88 minutes in controlled-bf16-2; fixed at 2^-23 it takes 2 rounds and 53 s and changes the matrix by 4.00%, and layer 1's attention by 11.7%; by this rule the feed-forward ends at 2^-15 after 10 rounds and 268 s with 2.21% changed and the attention at 2^-11 after 3 rounds and 24 s with 0.97% (records/development/2026-11-10-controlled-training/back-behind-halved.out, position2-behind-halved.out, and the -ridge-23 records beside them; the rule first declared, a projection on the rounds left, took 19 rounds and 474 s for 2.27%: choose-behind.out). It bounds the solver's work, not the trace: whether a written matrix is inside is read from the merge.
ridge_of_a_bringing_back.scales_with: how the stiffness of the bounds that are passed at a matrix compares with its unit, and the rounds allowed

passes_of_a_bringing_back.derivation: 10 passes of 40 iterations of the linear solve each. A cap on the splitting of one round's step, not a bound on the trace: a step cut short is a less well aimed step, and whether the written matrix is inside is read from the merge. The same 400 iterations as 5 passes of 80 take more rounds and leave a larger change at two ridges and on both solvers (records/development/2026-11-10-speed-review/calibration/, weight-research-perfomance: from 2^-17, 3 rounds and 2.28% against 5 rounds and 2.33%). At the smallest ridge with both merges held, 1 pass of 80 has not ended after 12 rounds and 80 passes leave the first round 6.46 outside where 5 leave 0.019, which is not explained (back-behind-ridge-23-passes-1.jsonl, -passes-80.out). It was 80 passes in controlled-bf16-2, set at the floor's ridge on one case.
passes_of_a_bringing_back.scales_with: how far the aim of a round's step moves from pass to pass at that matrix, which is not understood past the first passes

rounds_of_a_bringing_back.derivation: 40, the cap of a stage's rounds (rounds_of_a_stage). The 17 runs on the case that ended controlled-bf16-1 took three to eight rounds. A bringing back that reaches the cap, or in which no part of a step leaves less outside, ends outside, and the record says which; the matrix is then left as it stood.
rounds_of_a_bringing_back.scales_with: how much of what a round's writing leaves over lands on bounds that are full

drawing_in_behind.derivation: No number is set. Where the engine reads the layer's last merge outside behind a written feed-forward, each bound the solve works to there is drawn in to limit * (1 - d)^2, with d the root of what the engine read over that bound less the root of what the solve read, where that is positive, the largest over the three groups and all the fitting answers together. On the model controlled-bf16-2 left the largest d is 0.177 and the two readings of the furthest parts agree to four digits (after-check.out). The reference's bounds are not changed by this: what is accepted is the engine's reading against them.
drawing_in_behind.scales_with: how many rows the engine reads together at a layer and how near a rounding their states lie

prediction.expected_observation: The reference and the own-answer floors, made here by the same commands from the same observations, are controlled-bf16-2's to the last digit; a difference would be reported before any matrix is written. The build: layer 0's attention trains as it did (about 0.77 of its tube loss left). Layer 0's feed-forward arrives outside, is brought back inside both its own merge and the layer's last in about 19 rounds, the ridge ending near 2^-17, with about 2.3% of the matrix changed, and keeps no pull (about 0.91 left); the engine's own output behind it is inside, at once or after the bounds are drawn in. The sweep then passes its third matrix, which neither sweep before it did. Past that nothing has been read: most matrices are expected to arrive outside a bound an earlier change put them past, to be brought back with between 1% and a few percent of the matrix changed, and to keep little pull under the allowances as they are, so the tube loss left at the last merge is expected nearer 0.9 than 0.5 of the original; no record supports a sharper number, and this is the weakest part of the prediction. The sweep is still more likely than not to end before its last matrix: at a bringing back that does not end inside in its rounds (the rule has been run on two matrices, 6144 and 2048 wide, and not at 12288), at an engine reading behind a feed-forward that stays outside, or where the card's 16 GB are not enough. At about 5 minutes an attention matrix and 12 a feed-forward at layer 0, and twice that at the 20 widest, the build takes 12 to 20 hours. If it finishes, the replay and the own answers are expected as controlled-bf16-2 declared them: the replay not passing on every bound, the wrong group's own trace moving toward the correct pattern where a move is asked by less than the replay reads.
prediction.failures_only: Per merge and family, every cell outside its bound or budget with its size, group, place and whether a move is asked there, for the replay and for the own answers; every matrix taken back or left unchanged with why; every answer that ran into the limit. Per wrong answer, its fields before and after and where its own trace lies against the two patterns, beside the verdicts. Every bringing back with its rounds and what it left; every pull taken back with why and toward which matrix; where the engine's reading of a matrix's own merge differs from the solve's.

would_weaken_it: The hypothesis: the edited model's own answers carry the wrong group's trace into the correct pattern's resolution over the divergence with every budget held, and what those answers write is no nearer the correct calculation. By Marcos's direction that does not judge the training, but it would say the recurring difference in the trace is not what carries the capability. The construction, not the hypothesis: the sweep ends outside a bound within the first layers; or most matrices are left as they stand once the first bound is filled, so that the model barely differs from the original; or the replay's tube loss on the unused answers is not less than the original file's reading leaves although the fitting answers' is; or the own answers' tube loss is not below what the original file's second answers read with nothing changed; or the own answers move as far to the side as along the gap again. Any of these means the bounds as built do not carry from the fitted rows to the model's own computation, or leave the solver no room in the file's format, and the run then does not test the hypothesis. The prediction about the floors: the original file's reading lying outside a sampling bound of its own recorded rows at many cells would say the reading is not the recorded computation, and would be found and reported before any matrix is written. The solver's claim, which this run tests at every matrix: the engine reads a written matrix's own merge outside a bound that the solve read inside. That would say the rows are not multiplied the way tube.multiplied takes them at that matrix, and is reported at the position where it happens. The solver's claims this run tests: that a feed-forward's solve reads the layer's last merge as the engine does (weakened by an engine reading behind a written feed-forward that stays outside after the bounds are drawn in), and that the stepped ridge brings back what arrives outside (weakened by a bringing back that uses its rounds at the smallest ridge). Neither is the hypothesis: a sweep that ends early on either says the configuration is not there yet, and the record says where.
inputs_read_for_what: controlled-bf16-1/baseline and controlled-bf16-1/own/original are the observations of the original file this run is counted from (rule, original_observations). controlled-bf16-2/recorder-qualification is the byte comparison that qualifies the recorder's early stop this run's passes ask for, made on card 0 for the installed recorder (recorder_revision); controlled-bf16-2/result.json is where the last sweep ended, which this run's changes answer. No bound, floor or budget of this run comes from either.
